recognition: Recognized as UCI Parkinson's Telemonitoring (UCI 189) from the supplied documentation. No remembered prior-study result is claimed or used.
summary: Revise and retain I1 as a proposal for a repeatability-aware voice-change alert study. The supplied dataset contains 5,875 recordings from 42 people, but does not identify same-session replicates or provide an independently observed UPDRS score at every recording. The returned pair-gap count describes schedule density only; it cannot validate repeatability or clinical alerts. The limited Crossref results do not establish an exact prior match or world-literature novelty.

candidates.title: Replicate-aware voice change alerts
candidates.question: For a remote-monitoring session, does averaging three standardized home voice recordings improve detection of clinically anchored within-person motor change compared with the first recording, at the same false-alert rate?
candidates.new_claim: A replicate-based session estimate may separate short-term recording variability from persistent voice change enough to improve alert reliability. This is a proposal, not a finding in the supplied data.
candidates.input_delta: Adds same-session repeats, a fixed aggregation rule, and a clinical alert comparison. Supplied rows lack replicate/session identifiers and a controlled repeat protocol.
candidates.domain_value: Helps decide whether one voice capture is adequate or whether additional captures should be requested before acting on a change alert.
assumptions: Motor status is effectively unchanged during a replicate set collected minutes apart.
Prompt, microphone position, and recording procedure can be maintained at home.
The clinical comparison uses independently observed motor UPDRS assessments; interpolated labels are not independent clinical observations.
Clinicians prespecify the clinically meaningful score-change threshold, and alert cutoffs are selected using separate development participants before held-out evaluation.
candidates.variables_and_units: Independent unit: participant, with sessions nested within participant. Collect three recordings minutes apart per session using the same task and setup; compare the first recording with the arithmetic mean of all three. Acoustic feature units are unspecified in the supplied documentation. Record follow-up time in days and independently observed clinician motor UPDRS in score points. Outcomes are within-session feature dispersion and held-out sensitivity for a prespecified clinically meaningful score change at a fixed false-alert rate.
candidates.testable_prediction: In participant-held-out validation, the three-recording mean will have lower within-session acoustic dispersion and higher sensitivity for prespecified independently observed motor-UPDRS change than the first recording, at the same prespecified false-alert rate.
candidates.alternative: Replicate differences mostly reflect real short-term symptom or medication-state fluctuation; averaging removes useful signal and does not improve or worsens detection of clinical change.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect three fixed-task recordings minutes apart at each home session, repeat sessions over follow-up, and obtain independently observed clinician motor-UPDRS assessments at prespecified visits. Prespecify the clinically meaningful score-change threshold with clinicians and fit the alert cutoff using separate development participants. In held-out participants compare the first recording with the three-recording mean at the same false-alert rate, with participant-level uncertainty. Record medication timing/state and setup conditions to assess alternative sources of within-session variation.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Only a recording schedule-density check is feasible using subject# and test_time. No same-session repeatability, source attribution, or clinical alert validation is possible because replicate/session IDs and independent UPDRS labels at each recording are absent.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective sessions with three same-task recordings minutes apart, recording/session IDs, setup metadata, medication timing/state, repeated sessions per participant, and time-aligned independently observed clinician motor-UPDRS scores at clinical visits.
candidates.failure_condition: The proposal is unsupported for this use if the mean fails to reduce within-session dispersion or improve held-out sensitivity at equal false-alert rate, or if any apparent benefit disappears under participant-held-out validation.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for Parkinson home/remote voice studies directly comparing single recordings with same-session replicate aggregation for test-retest reliability or clinically anchored change alerts.

candidates.title: Separate medication-state response from progression
candidates.question: Do within-person voice measurements distinguish acute clinician-confirmed medication ON/OFF motor state from slower progression?
candidates.new_claim: A within-person voice signature might track acute motor-state changes separately from slower baseline trajectory; medication timing and ON/OFF status are absent from supplied variables.
candidates.input_delta: Adds timed medication-state labels and paired clinical assessments, changing the target from interpolated-score prediction to separation of acute state response from longitudinal change.
candidates.domain_value: Could prevent an acute medication fluctuation from being interpreted as disease progression and guide dose-aligned voice follow-up.
assumptions: Clinician-confirmed ON/OFF state can be measured alongside voice in the same participant.
Task, time of day, and setup can be held stable or recorded.
Any voice composite and its direction are frozen before participant-held-out validation.
candidates.variables_and_units: Participant-level paired ON/OFF sessions; categorical clinician-confirmed medication state; elapsed time since dose in hours; acoustic features in documented units (unspecified); observed motor UPDRS in score points; follow-up time in days. Compare within-person ON/OFF voice-feature differences with matched same-state temporal pairs.
candidates.testable_prediction: A composite defined in discovery participants will show a reproducible within-person association with observed motor-UPDRS difference across ON/OFF pairs in held-out participants, beyond matched same-state pairs and follow-up time.
candidates.alternative: Voice variation is dominated by recording/task variation or slower disease differences and has no stable acute state signal after within-person pairing.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect repeated voice and observed motor-UPDRS assessments in confirmed ON/OFF states with fixed task/setup; match same-state comparisons by time of day and follow-up interval; validate the frozen composite by participant. The supplied dataset has no medication-state field and cannot test medication effects.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No direct medication-state test: dose timing and ON/OFF labels are absent.
candidates.required_new_data: Repeated voice captures paired with confirmed ON/OFF state, dose and elapsed-time metadata, observed motor scores, and standardized task/setup and time-of-day records.
candidates.failure_condition: Fails if the frozen composite does not distinguish ON/OFF motor-score changes from matched same-state variation in held-out participants, or if association is accounted for by time or recording conditions.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for paired Parkinson medication ON/OFF studies using repeated home/remote voice measurements and observed motor scores.

candidates.title: Use voice variability to trigger symptom check-ins
candidates.question: Does within-day voice variability identify patient-reported motor-fluctuation episodes well enough to trigger an extra check-in more efficiently than fixed-time sampling?
candidates.new_claim: Within-day acoustic dispersion may signal a fluctuating symptom day rather than only poor recording quality; a burden-matched trigger policy can test whether it helps remote follow-up.
candidates.input_delta: Adds repeated daily recordings and contemporaneous symptom reports, evaluating a sampling decision rather than UPDRS score prediction.
candidates.domain_value: Could request extra symptom assessment selectively on likely fluctuation days while preserving event detection at lower monitoring burden.
assumptions: Patients can provide time-stamped fluctuation reports with adequate completion.
Recordings and reports can be scheduled within day; medication timing and setup are recorded.
Check-in burden can be represented by counts per participant-week.
candidates.variables_and_units: Decision unit: participant-day, with recordings nested within participant and day. Collect morning and later-day samples; calculate within-day dispersion of a prespecified voice composite. Record fluctuation event as time-stamped categorical patient report and check-ins as counts. Compare event detection at equal check-in counts per participant-week.
candidates.testable_prediction: At equal check-in count per participant-week, a frozen high-dispersion trigger will detect more patient-reported fluctuation days than fixed-time sampling in held-out participants.
candidates.alternative: Dispersion is mostly caused by setup or medication timing and does not track reported fluctuations; fixed-time sampling performs as well or better.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect time-stamped repeated home recordings, brief symptom reports, medication timing, and setup metadata. Freeze a dispersion threshold in development data, then compare event sensitivity at matched check-in burden against fixed sampling in held-out participants; account for repeated participant-days.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No direct policy test: the table has no same-day marker, symptom diary, medication timing, or check-in outcomes.
candidates.required_new_data: Multiple daily recordings, contemporaneous fluctuation reports, medication timing/state, setup metadata, and check-in burden/outcome in a prospective cohort.
candidates.failure_condition: Unsupported if the trigger does not detect more fluctuation days than fixed sampling at matched burden in participant-held-out evaluation, or if the signal is explained by setup or medication timing.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for Parkinson home voice monitoring using within-day acoustic variability to trigger symptom assessment or adaptive sampling at matched monitoring burden.

acceptance: Report the pair-gap results only as schedule density, never as same-session replicate evidence.

Use independently observed clinical scores, a prespecified clinically meaningful change threshold, a development-set alert cutoff, participant-held-out validation, and an equal false-alert comparison.
Compare the returned Crossref records with the proposed relation while respecting title-only and limited-coverage evidence.
Label the idea proposal-only unless a returned result directly tests its core prediction.
task.proposed_computation: Completed broker request R1_gap_counts: exhaustive within-person distinct-row pair counts at absolute test_time gaps <=1 day and <=7 days. It is descriptive schedule information only.
task.proposed_search: Completed Crossref request R1_crossref_repeatability with query: (Parkinson OR Parkinson's) AND (voice OR speech) AND (home OR remote) AND (repeatability OR test-retest OR replicate) AND (clinical change OR motor score). Returned index coverage is limited; several records are reviews/decision letters, and most results provide titles and dates only.

critique: The clinically meaningful change threshold and alert-cutoff fitting rule were initially underspecified. The final protocol requires clinician prespecification and selection of the alert cutoff in separate development participants.

A session mean can average away genuine minute-scale symptom or medication variation. Same-session repeats minutes apart, medication timing/state, fixed task/setup, and an independent clinical anchor are needed to distinguish this alternative.
Nearby rows in the current table need not be same-session recordings. The returned gap counts establish schedule density only and cannot estimate measurement error or validate alert performance.

final.what_changed: The core candidate is retained but its protocol is revised: clinicians must define the meaningful score-change threshold, a separate participant development set must determine the alert cutoff, and final comparison is participant-held-out at an equal false-alert rate. The compute result changes only the schedule-feasibility description; it does not update the repeatability or clinical-validity prediction. Search results leave literature novelty unresolved.
final.what_is_known: The dataset is UCI Parkinson's Telemonitoring (UCI 189), with 5,875 recordings from 42 participants over approximately six months and linearly interpolated motor_UPDRS and total_UPDRS targets. The broker counted 14,616 within-person distinct-row pairs at gaps <=1 day and 31,582 at gaps <=7 days; these are calendar-gap pairs, not verified same-session replicates. Crossref returned eight records: six review/decision-letter records for a hands-feet wireless-device test-retest paper, one unrelated pupillometry abstract, and one title-only record on self-perceptions of Parkinson speech, voice, and swallowing. No returned result establishes the proposed home voice replicate comparison.
final.what_is_new_hypothesis: Beyond the supplied benchmark framing, the study tests an operational measurement choice: whether averaging three standardized captures minutes apart improves clinically anchored motor-change alert sensitivity over the first capture at the same false-alert rate, and whether any gain coincides with lower within-session acoustic dispersion.
final.falsifier: The proposed use is unsupported if averaging three captures does not lower within-session dispersion or fails to improve held-out sensitivity at the same prespecified false-alert rate, or if the apparent gain disappears with participant-held-out validation.
final.minimum_next_test: Run a prospective pilot with three same-task home voice captures minutes apart per session, repeated sessions per participant, setup and medication timing/state metadata, and time-aligned independently observed clinician motor-UPDRS visits. Prespecify the meaningful score-change threshold, choose alert cutoffs in separate development participants, then compare first-capture and three-capture-mean alerts in held-out participants at equal false-alert rate with participant-level uncertainty. Use pilot repeatability and outcome variability to size a later confirmatory cohort.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The supplied documentation already identifies regression prediction of interpolated UPDRS from voice measures as the dataset's main aim. The returned Crossref search includes a title concerning test-retest reliability of hands-feet wireless motor measures in Parkinson telemonitoring, but it does not establish a voice-replicate study; the remaining returned Parkinson speech/voice title is about self-perceptions, and the pupillometry result is outside this domain. Search relevance and coverage are limited, with title-only records and no full-text review, so no claim of world-literature novelty is supported.
final.novelty_status: The idea adds a new measurement and decision comparison to the supplied input by testing one capture versus a three-capture mean for clinically anchored alerting. Novelty in published work is unverified; the limited Crossref results neither confirm nor rule out prior direct studies.
limitations: The current dataset cannot test the central hypothesis because it lacks replicate/session identifiers, medication and setup metadata, and independent clinical labels at each recording.
The pair-gap calculation is a schedule-density check and says nothing about repeatability, biological fluctuation, or clinical performance.
The Crossref search is limited and several results are title-only or publication-process records; absence of a direct match is not evidence of absence.
The proposed comparison requires a prospectively collected cohort and does not establish causal benefit from averaging.
